content: Ampicillin has been shown in laboratory studies to be effective against certain bacterial strains, but its clinical effectiveness for infections outside those specified in the Indications and Usage section has not been established. The following Gram-positive organisms have demonstrated susceptibility to Ampicillin in vitro: hemolytic and non-hemolytic streptococci, Bacillus anthracis, Listeria monocytogenes, and most strains of enterococci. The following Gram-negative organisms have also shown susceptibility to Ampicillin in vitro: Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Neisseria meningitidis, Proteus mirabilis, and many strains of Salmonella, Shigella, and Escherichia coli. It is important to note that Ampicillin is not resistant to degradation by penicillinase enzymes. For susceptibility testing, Ampicillin Susceptibility Test Discs containing 10 µg of the drug should be used to determine the in vitro susceptibility of bacteria to Ampicillin for Injection, USP.
